plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit remaining tech/semiconductor holdings (QQQI, QQQ, SMH, CRWD).
Buy Microsoft (MSFT) as a quality tech addition.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces risk significantly.
It aims for steady, low-drawdown performance.
conservative.read: This conservative approach focuses on capital preservation. Expect lower monthly returns, around 1.5%, with significantly reduced drawdown risk. It prioritizes safety over aggressive growth.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to minimal levels.
Sell income (QQQI) and broad index (QQQ) holdings.
Exit semiconductor exposure (SMH).
Buy Snowflake (SNOW) as a quality tech addition.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
It aims for steady, risk-first growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces concentration and leverage while adding quality names. Drawdowns are expected to be moderate.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to target levels.
Sell income (QQQI) and broad index (QQQ) holdings.
Exit semiconductor exposure (SMH).
Buy Snowflake (SNOW) as a high-conviction addition.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration.
It accepts higher potential upside and significantly larger drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets substantial growth, around 4% per month, by leaning into leverage and high-conviction names. Expect amplified gains and losses, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potentially large drawdowns.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta tech (QQQ, CRWD, SMH).
Increase income ETF (QQQI) to a significant allocation.
Reduce broad index (SPY) exposure.
This plan prioritizes generating steady monthly income.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable distributions.
Growth potential is secondary to income generation.
income.read: This income-focused plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions, targeting around 1% per month. It shifts capital to income-generating ETFs and reduces volatile assets. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market selloffs, and distributions are not guaranteed.
